div.div:
Hardware-Aware Scheduling (NVIDIA Blackwell/Vera Rubin)
As AI hardware becomes more specialized, custom schedulers can be programmed to look for specific hardware features that Kubernetes doesn't natively track well:
RDMA/InfiniBand: Scheduling pods on nodes that share the same high-speed InfiniBand switch.
Low-precision support: Directing specific workloads only to nodes whose GPUs support the formats they need, e.g. FP8 (Hopper and newer) or FP4 (Blackwell).

li.p: Standard Method: Use Taints, Tolerations, and Labels.
The "Workaround": You manually label your Blackwell nodes with gpu-gen=blackwell and your InfiniBand nodes with network=infiniband. You then add nodeSelectors to your AI pods.

The Failure Point: This works well! This is actually how most people start. The custom scheduler only becomes necessary when you have thousands of nodes and you don't want to manually manage labels and selectors for every single hardware iteration (FP8, HBM3, NVLink v4, etc.).
